effect: The result connects breathing and circulation: oxygen enters the blood in the lungs, while carbon dioxide moves into the lungs to be breathed out. The route also shows blood returning to the heart between the lungs and body.
reaction: The complete route was satisfying, and the return to the heart between the lungs and body clarified the circuit.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the breathing lungs to circulation was most worthwhile because it explained gas exchange and traced the blood route through the lungs and body.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making circulation was the least engaging moment because the heart pumping blood through vessels was predictable, although the explanation of a returning circuit and cells was useful.

surprise.text: The full route clarified that blood returns to the heart after passing through the lungs before going to the body.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary: each pair had a clear purpose, though the menu supplied the compatible combinations rather than leaving me to discover them.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the explanations connect familiar organs into a system, and I am curious how oxygen reaches and supports the arm's muscles. The chapter explains gas exchange but has not yet shown what muscles do with the oxygen.
